On the Analytic Invariants and Semiroots of Plane BranchesThanks: The first author was partially supported by CAPES and the second one by CNPq-Brazil.Thanks: Corresponding author: Hernandes, M. E.; email: mehernandes@uem.br

Abstract

The value semigroup of a kk-semiroot CkC_{k} of a plane branch CC allows us to recover part of the value semigroup Γ=⟨v0,…,vg⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle of CC, that is, it is related to topological invariants of CC. In this paper we consider the set of values of differentials Λk\Lambda_{k} of CkC_{k}, that is an analytical invariant, and we show how it determine part of the set of values of differentials Λ\Lambda of CC. As a consequence, in a fixed topological class, we relate the Tjurina number τ\tau of CC with the Tjurina number of CkC_{k}. In particular, we show that τ≤μ−3​ng−24​μg−1\tau\leq\mu-\frac{3n_{g}-2}{4}\mu_{g-1} where ng=g​c​d​(v0,…,vg−1)n_{g}=gcd(v_{0},\ldots,v_{g-1}), μ\mu and μg−1\mu_{g-1} denote the Milnor number of CC and Cg−1C_{g-1} respectively. If ng=2n_{g}=2, we have that τ=μ−μg−1\tau=\mu-\mu_{g-1} for any curve in the topological class determined by Γ\Gamma that is a generalization of a result obtained by Luengo and Pfister.

2010 Mathematics Subject Classification: 14H20 (primary), 32S10 (secondary)

keywords: Plane curves, Semiroots, Analytic Invariants.

1 Introduction

Given f∈ℂ​{x,y}f\in\mathbb{C}\{x,y\} irreducible the equation f=0f=0 define a germ of irreducible plane curve, or a branch, CfC_{f}.

The topological class of CfC_{f} can be totaly characterized by numerical data: by the characteristic exponents of a Puiseux parametrization, the value semigroup Γf\Gamma_{f}, the multiplicity sequence in the canonical resolution, for instance. All of these numerical invariants determine each other and can be easily computed.

The value semigroup Γf⊆ℕ\Gamma_{f}\subseteq\mathbb{N} admits a conductor μf\mu_{f} that is, μf−1∉Γf\mu_{f}-1\not\in\Gamma_{f} and μf+ℕ⊆Γf\mu_{f}+\mathbb{N}\subseteq\Gamma_{f}. So, Γf\Gamma_{f} is determined by the finite set ℕ∖Γf\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{f} and μf\mu_{f} is a topological invariant that coincide with the Milnor number of ff, i.e., μf=dimℂℂ​{x,y}⟨fx,fy⟩\mu_{f}=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\frac{\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}}{\langle f_{x},f_{y}\rangle}.

On the other hand, it is not so easy to compute analytical invariants and to describe relation among them. In [HH3], the set Λf\Lambda_{f} of values of differentials was the principal analytical invariant and ingredient considered to obtain normal forms with respect to the analytical equivalence of plane branches. The set Λf\Lambda_{f} is related with the Tjurina number τf=dimℂℂ​{x,y}⟨f,fx,fy⟩\tau_{f}=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\frac{\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}}{\langle f,f_{x},f_{y}\rangle}, another analytical invariant of CfC_{f}, by the formula τf=μf−♯⁡(Λf∖Γf)\tau_{f}=\mu_{f}-\sharp(\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f}).

Up to analytical equivalence any plane curve can be defined by a Weierstrass polynomial f∈ℂ​{x}​[y]f\in\mathbb{C}\{x\}[y] and many topological aspects of CfC_{f} can be studied by a set of monic irreducible polynomials fk∈ℂ​{x}​[y], 0≤k<gf_{k}\in\mathbb{C}\{x\}[y],\ 0\leq k<g with d​e​gy​(fk)=v0ekdeg_{y}(f_{k})=\frac{v_{0}}{e_{k}}, called semiroots of ff, such that νf​(fk):=dimℂℂ​{x,y}⟨f,fk⟩=vk+1\nu_{f}(f_{k}):=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\frac{\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}}{\langle f,f_{k}\rangle}=v_{k+1} where Γf=⟨v0,v1,…,vg⟩\Gamma_{f}=\langle v_{0},v_{1},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle, d​e​gy​(f)=v0=dimℂℂ​{x,y}⟨f,x⟩deg_{y}(f)=v_{0}=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\frac{\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}}{\langle f,x\rangle} and ei=g​c​d​(v0,…,vi)e_{i}=gcd(v_{0},\ldots,v_{i}) (see Section 2).

Several authors have considered semiroots in different contexts. For instance, Zariski in [Z3] considered semiroots given by minimal polynomial of truncation of Puiseux parametrization of CfC_{f} to compute the minimal set of generators of the semigroup. Abhyankar in [Ab] presented an irreducibility criterion for elements in ℂ​{x}​[y]\mathbb{C}\{x\}[y] using approximate roots that are particular cases of semiroots. In [Y], Yavorski gave a method to construct a miniversal family of polynomials in ℂ⁡[x,y]\mathbb{C}[x,y] that define branches with a fixed semigroup considering semiroots. Popescu in [Pop] presented several local properties of semiroots including a proof of the Embedding Line Theorem as an application.

It is possible to relate the topological data of CfC_{f} with the corresponding data of the branch CkC_{k} associated to fkf_{k}. For example, we have

Γf=ek​Γk+⟨vk+1,…,vg⟩andμf−1=ek​(μk−1)+∑j=k+1g(nj−1)​vj,\Gamma_{f}=e_{k}\Gamma_{k}+\langle v_{k+1},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle\ \ \ \mbox{and}\ \ \ \mu_{f}-1=e_{k}(\mu_{k}-1)+\sum_{j=k+1}^{g}\left(n_{j}-1\right)v_{j},

where nj=ej−1ejn_{j}=\frac{e_{j-1}}{e_{j}}, Γk\Gamma_{k} is the value semigroup and μk\mu_{k} is the Milnor number of CkC_{k}.

The aim of this work is to study relations among the analytical invariants Λf\Lambda_{f}, τf\tau_{f}, Λk\Lambda_{k} and τk\tau_{k} associated to CfC_{f} and CkC_{k} respectively. For this purpose, in Section 3 we explore the logarithmic differential forms along a curve and we revisit results of Briançon, Maisonobe and Torrelli (see [BMT]) about some magic matrix associated to a plane curve and its Jacobian ideal.

In the Section 4 we describe a common subset of Λ∖Γ\Lambda\setminus\Gamma shared by any plane branch CC that admits a fixed semiroot fkf_{k} and consequently we can relate the Tjurina number τ\tau of CC with the Tjurina number τk\tau_{k} of CkC_{k}. More explicitly, for 0≤k<g0\leq k<g we get τ≤μ−μk−ek+1​(nk+1−2)​τk\tau\leq\mu-\mu_{k}-e_{k+1}(n_{k+1}-2)\tau_{k}.

Dimca and Greuel in [DG] conjectured that 34​μ≤τ\frac{3}{4}\mu\leq\tau for any plane curve. This question motivated several works, see [AABM], [GH], [Wan] for a proof in the irreducible case and [Al] for any plane curve. So, for k=g−1k=g-1 we get τ≤μ−μg−1−(ng−2)​τg−1≤μ−(3​ng−24)​μg−1\tau\leq\mu-\mu_{g-1}-(n_{g}-2)\tau_{g-1}\leq\mu-(\frac{3n_{g}-2}{4})\mu_{g-1}, that is an upper bound for τ\tau for any plane branch in a fixed topological class.

Considering the topological class given by Γ=⟨v0,…,vg⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle with ng=g​c​d​(v0,…,vg−1)=2n_{g}=gcd(v_{0},\ldots,v_{g-1})=2, in Section 5 we show that τ\tau is constant and equal to μ−μg−1\mu-\mu_{g-1} for any plane branch that admits the semigroup Γ\Gamma. This result is trivial if g=1g=1 and it was showed by Luengo and Pfister for g=2g=2 in [LP].

2 Plane branches and semiroots

In what follows we recall some classical result about plane curves using the presentation of [BK], [H] and [Z3].

Let ℂ​{x,y}\mathbb{C}\{x,y\} be the ring of analytic power series ring in xx and yy over ℂ\mathbb{C} and ℳ=⟨x,y⟩\mathcal{M}=\langle x,y\rangle its maximal ideal. Let Cf∈(ℂ2,0)C_{f}\in(\mathbb{C}^{2},0) be a singular irreducible plane curve (a plane branch) defined by f=0f=0, where f∈ℳn∖ℳn+1f\in\mathcal{M}^{n}\setminus\mathcal{M}^{n+1} is irreducible and n>1n>1 is its multiplicity.

We say that CfC_{f} and ChC_{h} are analytically equivalent if there exist neighborhoods U,V⊆(ℂ2,0)U,V\subseteq(\mathbb{C}^{2},0) and an analytic isomorphism Ψ:(ℂ2,0)→(ℂ2,0)\Psi:(\mathbb{C}^{2},0)\rightarrow(\mathbb{C}^{2},0) such that Ψ⁡(U∩Cf)=V∩Ch\Psi(U\cap C_{f})=V\cap C_{h}. If Ψ\Psi is just a homeomorphism we say that CfC_{f} and ChC_{h} are topologically equivalent.

The above remarks indicate how some topological data of a branch and of their semiroots are related. More delicate question is: How we can relate analytical invariants of CfC_{f} and CkC_{k}? Investigating this question is one of the aim of this work.

In the next section we will present results about some analytical invariants of a plane branch associated with differential forms that play an important role in the main results of this work.

3 Differential forms on CfC_{f}

Let Ω1=ℂ⁡{x,y}​d​x+ℂ⁡{x,y}​d​y\Omega^{1}=\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}dx+\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}dy be the ℂ​{x,y}\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}-module of holomorphic forms on ℂ2\mathbb{C}^{2}.

Given f∈ℂ​{x,y}f\in\mathbb{C}\{x,y\} we denote d​f=fx​d​x+fy​d​ydf=f_{x}dx+f_{y}dy and ℱ⁡(f)=f⋅Ω1+ℂ⁡{x,y}⋅d​f\mathcal{F}(f)=f\cdot\Omega^{1}+\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}\cdot df. The Kähler differential module of the branch CfC_{f} is the 𝒪f\mathcal{O}_{f}-module Ωf:=Ω𝒪f/ℂ=Ω1ℱ⁡(f)\Omega_{f}:=\Omega_{\mathcal{O}_{f}/\mathbb{C}}=\frac{\Omega^{1}}{\mathcal{F}(f)}. If CfC_{f} is singular then Ωf\Omega_{f} has a non trivial torsion submodule 𝒯f={ω∈Ωf;hω=0for some 0≠h∈𝒪f}\mathcal{T}_{f}=\{\omega\in\Omega_{f};\ h\omega=0\ \mbox{for some}\ 0\neq h\in\mathcal{O}_{f}\} and ℓ⁡(𝒯f)=τf=dimℂℂ​{x,y}⟨f,fx,fy⟩\ell(\mathcal{T}_{f})=\tau_{f}=\dim_{\mathbb{C}}\frac{\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}}{\langle f,f_{x},f_{y}\rangle} (see [Z2] for instance).

Considering a parametrization (x⁡(t),y⁡(t))∈ℂ⁡{t}×ℂ⁡{t}(x(t),y(t))\in\mathbb{C}\{t\}\times\mathbb{C}\{t\} of CfC_{f} and the identification 𝒪f≈ℂ⁡{x⁡(t),y⁡(t)}\mathcal{O}_{f}\approx\mathbb{C}\{x(t),y(t)\} we define the 𝒪f\mathcal{O}_{f}-homomorphism

Υ:Ωf→ℂ​{t}≈𝒪¯fA⁡(x,y)​d​x+B⁡(x,y)​d​y↦t⋅(A⁡(x⁡(t),y⁡(t))⋅x′​(t)+B⁡(x⁡(t),y⁡(t))⋅y′​(t)),\begin{array}[]{cccc}\Upsilon:&\Omega_{f}&\rightarrow&\mathbb{C}\{t\}\approx\overline{\mathcal{O}}_{f}\\ &A(x,y)dx+B(x,y)dy&\mapsto&t\cdot(A(x(t),y(t))\cdot x^{\prime}(t)+B(x(t),y(t))\cdot y^{\prime}(t)),\end{array}

and ker⁡(Υ)=𝒯f\ker(\Upsilon)=\mathcal{T}_{f}.

The set Λf={νf(ω):=ordt(Υ(ω));0¯≠ω¯∈Ωf𝒯f}\Lambda_{f}=\{\nu_{f}(\omega):=ord_{t}(\Upsilon(\omega));\ \overline{0}\neq\overline{\omega}\in\frac{\Omega_{f}}{\mathcal{T}_{f}}\} is an analytical invariant of CfC_{f} and Γf∖{0}={νf(dh); 0≠h∈𝒪f∩⟨t⟩}⊆Λf\Gamma_{f}\setminus\{0\}=\{\nu_{f}(dh);\ 0\neq h\in\mathcal{O}_{f}\cap\langle t\rangle\}\subseteq\Lambda_{f}. The set Λf\Lambda_{f} has a prominent role in many works (see [De] and [HH3] for instance) and it is related with the Tjurina number τf\tau_{f} of CfC_{f} by the relation τf=μf−♯⁡(Λf∖Γf)\tau_{f}=\mu_{f}-\sharp(\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f}). In [HH2] we found an algorithm to compute the set Λf\Lambda_{f} for any irreducible curve plane or not and all possible set of values of differentials for plane curves with a fixed semigroup.

According to Saito (see [S]) an element W∈1f​Ω1W\in\frac{1}{f}\Omega^{1} is a logarithmic form along CfC_{f} if there exist ϖ∈Ω1\varpi\in\Omega^{1}, P,Q∈ℂ⁡{x,y},Q∉⟨f⟩P,Q\in\mathbb{C}\{x,y\},Q\not\in\langle f\rangle such that Q​W=P​d​f+f​ϖfQW=\frac{Pdf+f\varpi}{f}. Saito denotes Ω⁡(l​o​g​Cf)={W;W​is a logarithmic form along​Cf}\Omega(log\ C_{f})=\{W;\ W\ \mbox{is a logarithmic form along}\ C_{f}\} and motivated by this, in the sequel, we will consider the ℂ​{x,y}\mathbb{C}\{x,y\}-module f⋅Ω⁡(l​o​g​Cf)={f⋅W;W∈Ω⁡(l​o​g​Cf)}⊂Ω1f\cdot\Omega(log\ C_{f})=\{f\cdot W;\ W\in\Omega(log\ C_{f})\}\subset\Omega^{1}. It follows that 𝒯f=f⋅Ω⁡(l​o​g​Cf)ℱ⁡(f)\mathcal{T}_{f}=\frac{f\cdot\Omega(log\ C_{f})}{\mathcal{F}(f)}.

In section 2 of [S], Saito introduce the residue of a logarithmic form that can be defined considering f⋅Ω⁡(l​o​g​Cf)f\cdot\Omega(log\ C_{f}). More precisely, given ω∈f⋅Ω⁡(l​o​g​Cf)\omega\in f\cdot\Omega(log\ C_{f}) with Q​ω=P​d​f+f​ϖQ\omega=Pdf+f\varpi we call r​e​s​(ω)=P¯Q¯∈F​r​a​c​(𝒪f)res(\omega)=\frac{\overline{P}}{\overline{Q}}\in Frac(\mathcal{O}_{f}) the residue of ω\omega where F​r​a​c​(𝒪f)Frac({\mathcal{O}_{f}}) is the field of fraction of 𝒪f\mathcal{O}_{f}. We have that r​e​s​(ω)res(\omega) is well defined and ℛf:={r​e​s​(ω);ω∈f⋅Ω⁡(l​o​g​Cf)}⊇𝒪¯f\mathcal{R}_{f}:=\{res(\omega);\ \omega\in f\cdot\Omega(log\ C_{f})\}\supseteq\overline{\mathcal{O}}_{f}.

Pol (see Corollary 3.32, [Pol]) shows that Λf\Lambda_{f} determines and it is determined by the set Δf:={νf​(P)−νf​(Q);P¯Q¯∈ℛf}\Delta_{f}:=\{\nu_{f}(P)-\nu_{f}(Q);\ \frac{\overline{P}}{\overline{Q}}\in\mathcal{R}_{f}\}. 5 Branches with semigroup Γ=⟨v0,…,vg⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle and ng=2n_{g}=2

In [LP], Luengo and Pfister proof that in the topological class determined by semigroup Γ=⟨v0,v1,v2⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},v_{1},v_{2}\rangle with n2=G​C​D​(v0,v1)=2n_{2}=GCD(v_{0},v_{1})=2 the Tjurina number τf\tau_{f} is the same for any branch CfC_{f} belonging to it and τf=μf−(v02−1)​(v12−1)=μf−μ1\tau_{f}=\mu_{f}-\left(\frac{v_{0}}{2}-1\right)\left(\frac{v_{1}}{2}-1\right)=\mu_{f}-\mu_{1} where, as before, μ1\mu_{1} denote the Milnor number of the 11-semiroot f1f_{1}. Inspired by the result of Luengo and Pfister, Watari (see [Wat]) ask if the Tjurina number can be expressed using topological data for branches with semigroup Γ=⟨v0,v1,…,vg⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},v_{1},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle with ni=2n_{i}=2 for i=1,…,gi=1,\ldots,g.

In this section we will show that the inequality in Corollary 4.10 is sharp for any branch CfC_{f} in the equisingularity class determined by Γ=⟨v0,v1,…,vg⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},v_{1},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle with ng=2n_{g}=2, that is, τf=μf−μg−1\tau_{f}=\mu_{f}-\mu_{g-1}. In particular, we obtain a generalization of the result of Luengo-Pfister and an answer for a Watari’s question.

Notice that for g=1g=1 if n1=2n_{1}=2 then we get Γ=⟨2,v1⟩\Gamma=\langle 2,v_{1}\rangle and τf=μf=v1−1\tau_{f}=\mu_{f}=v_{1}-1 for any curve CfC_{f} with semigroup Γ\Gamma (see [Z2] for instance). So, in what follows we will suppose that g>1g>1.

Firstly we present a result for any branch with semigroup Γ=⟨v0,…,vg⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle without restriction on nin_{i}.

Proposition 5.1.

{λ∈Λf∖Γf;λ<vk+1}=ρk​(Λk∖Γk)​∪˙​{vk+1−ek​δk;δk∈ℕ∗∖Λk}.\{\lambda\in\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f};\ \lambda<v_{k+1}\}=\rho_{k}(\Lambda_{k}\setminus\Gamma_{k})\ \dot{\cup}\ \{v_{k+1}-e_{k}\delta_{k};\ \delta_{k}\in\mathbb{N}^{*}\setminus\Lambda_{k}\}.

As a consequence any branch with Γ=⟨v0,…,vg⟩\Gamma=\langle v_{0},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle and ng=2n_{g}=2 has the same Tjurina number and it can be expressed by means Γ\Gamma.

Theorem 5.2.

For any branch CfC_{f} in the topological class determined by Γf=⟨v0,…,vg⟩\Gamma_{f}=\langle v_{0},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle with ng=2n_{g}=2 we have that

Λf∖Γf=ρg−1​(Λg−1∖Γg−1)​∪˙​{vg−2​δ,δ∈ℕ∗∖Λg−1}​∪˙​{vg+2​δ;δ∈ℕ∖Γg−1}​and​♯​(Λf∖Γf)=μg−1.\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f}=\rho_{g-1}(\Lambda_{g-1}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1})\ \dot{\cup}\ \{v_{g}-2\delta,\ \delta\in\mathbb{N}^{*}\setminus\Lambda_{g-1}\}\ \dot{\cup}\ \{v_{g}+2\delta;\ \delta\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1}\}\ \ \mbox{and}\ \ \sharp(\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f})=\mu_{g-1}.

In particular, we have that τf=μf−μg−1.\tau_{f}=\mu_{f}-\mu_{g-1}.

Proof: Given Γf=⟨v0,…,vg⟩\Gamma_{f}=\langle v_{0},\ldots,v_{g}\rangle with ng=eg−1=2n_{g}=e_{g-1}=2 any vg<λ∉Γfv_{g}<\lambda\not\in\Gamma_{f} can be uniquely expressed as λ=vg+∑i=1g−1si​vi−s0​v0=vg+2​(∑i=1g−1si​vi2−s0​v02)\lambda=v_{g}+\sum_{i=1}^{g-1}s_{i}v_{i}-s_{0}v_{0}=v_{g}+2\left(\sum_{i=1}^{g-1}s_{i}\frac{v_{i}}{2}-s_{0}\frac{v_{0}}{2}\right) with 0≤si<ni0\leq s_{i}<n_{i} for i>0i>0 and s0≥0s_{0}\geq 0 (see Remark 2.1). In particular, ∑i=1g−1si​vi2−s0​v02∈ℕ∖Γg−1\sum_{i=1}^{g-1}s_{i}\frac{v_{i}}{2}-s_{0}\frac{v_{0}}{2}\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1} and any vg<λ∉Γfv_{g}<\lambda\not\in\Gamma_{f} is such that λ∈{vg+2​δ;δ∈ℕ∖Γg−1}\lambda\in\{v_{g}+2\delta;\ \delta\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1}\}, that is, {λ∈Λf∖Γf;λ>vg}⊂{vg+2​γ;γ∈ℕ∖Γg−1}\{\lambda\in\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f};\ \lambda>v_{g}\}\subset\{v_{g}+2\gamma;\ \gamma\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1}\}. Consequently, by (16) we have {λ∈Λf∖Γf;λ>vg}={vg+2​γ;γ∈ℕ∖Γg−1}\{\lambda\in\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f};\ \lambda>v_{g}\}=\{v_{g}+2\gamma;\ \gamma\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1}\}.

Now, by the previous proposition we get

Λf∖Γf=ρg−1​(Λg−1∖Γg−1)​∪˙​{vg−2​δ,δ∈ℕ∗∖Λg−1}​∪˙​{vg+2​γ;γ∈ℕ∖Γg−1}.\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f}=\rho_{g-1}(\Lambda_{g-1}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1})\ \dot{\cup}\ \{v_{g}-2\delta,\ \delta\in\mathbb{N}^{*}\setminus\Lambda_{g-1}\}\ \dot{\cup}\ \{v_{g}+2\gamma;\ \gamma\in\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1}\}.

As ♯​ρg−1​(Λg−1∖Γg−1)=♯⁡(Λg−1∖Γg−1)\sharp\rho_{g-1}(\Lambda_{g-1}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1})=\sharp(\Lambda_{g-1}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1}), and ♯⁡(ℕ∖Γg−1)=μg−12\sharp(\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1})=\frac{\mu_{g-1}}{2}, we obtain

♯⁡(Λf∖Γf)=♯⁡(Λg−1∖Γg−1)+♯⁡(ℕ∗∖Λg−1)+♯⁡(ℕ∖Γg−1)=2​♯​(ℕ∖Γg−1)=μg−1.\sharp(\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f})=\sharp(\Lambda_{g-1}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1})+\sharp(\mathbb{N}^{*}\setminus\Lambda_{g-1})+\sharp(\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1})=2\sharp(\mathbb{N}\setminus\Gamma_{g-1})=\mu_{g-1}.

In particular, τf=μf−♯⁡(Λf∖Γf)=μf−μg−1\tau_{f}=\mu_{f}-\sharp(\Lambda_{f}\setminus\Gamma_{f})=\mu_{f}-\mu_{g-1}.
